scope: This register records material changes to the official hosted-service legal documents. Spelling, formatting, and link corrections that do not change meaning are not separate entries.

changes: Specified the YouTube channel, video, playlist, publication, analytics, comment, and authorization information accessed and stored, with each category's purpose and recipients.
Explained how to request deletion of stored YouTube data, revoke access in OpenPost or Google security settings, and distinguish service deletion from deleting content on YouTube.

Linked YouTube export retention conditions and stated the seven-day direct-revocation or deletion-request deadline and the 30-day Google-revocation deadline. Described provider-cache expiry, profile refresh and the bounded NAS recovery-copy window.

Required recipients of exported YouTube API data, including CSV reports, to delete or refresh it within 30 calendar days of its last fetch or refresh from YouTube; downloading or copying does not restart that period.
Applied authorization, revocation, user-deletion, current-data display, and downstream-recipient obligations to exported copies outside OpenPost.
Disclosed separately optional native app analytics for screen visits, selected actions, device and app version facts, and sanitized JavaScript errors.
Documented per-server device consent, memory-only analytics state, and clearing pending events when consent, server, or account changes.
Clarified that Decline disables optional browser analytics and that cookie-free analytics requires a separate choice.
Disclosed that whole-account analytics stores bounded titles and text for eligible provider content published outside OpenPost so users can inspect evidence and prepare a reviewed repurpose draft.
Clarified that analytics inventory excludes raw provider responses, remote media bytes, credentials, bot secrets, and webhook secrets, while telemetry continues to exclude post text.
Added a separate, withdrawable browser analytics choice with persistent first-party, limited cookieless, and fully off modes.
Documented cross-subdomain first-party identity after permission, country derivation before raw IP discard, browser privacy signals, and the separate backend service-telemetry boundary.
Replaced the prior public-site-only Umami disclosure with the managed PostHog product, service, website, documentation, and error telemetry boundary.

Documented opaque signed-in identifiers, cookieless public analytics, memory-only browser persistence, disabled replay and autocapture, excluded content and credentials, retention, and the PostHog EU Cloud subprocessor.
Named the managed service's current data locations, service providers, user-directed recipients, and international-transfer facts.
Explained the managed human production-access boundary, routine recovery-copy window, and browser-local Image and Video Editor boundary.
Documented the automatic image-caption request, feedback recipient, stock-media providers, Paddle role, and current retention and browser-storage schedules.
Replaced the prior billing disclosure with Paddle's Merchant of Record role and retained the boundary for prior payment-provider records.
Added the operator identity, Portugal contact facts, policy-version behavior, and hosted-versus-self-hosted scope.
Added Paddle's Merchant of Record role, subscription and cancellation terms, the incorporated Refund Policy, and the operator and governing-law facts.
Clarified the hosted-service boundary and the acceptance version recorded by the application.
Published the first separate Refund Policy incorporated into the Terms, including the standard request window, statutory-rights boundary, exclusions, and Paddle processing path.

Published the first complete hosted-service Privacy Policy covering account, publishing, connected-account, security, billing, support, sharing, retention, browser storage, transfer, and user-rights categories.
Published the first complete hosted-service Terms of Service covering accounts, acceptable use, customer content, connected services, paid plans, availability, liability, termination, and changes.
